nary_nodes.label: Jewelry stolen from Lalique Museum
evidence: Burglars stole millions of dollars worth of jewelry from the museum of French luxury glassmaker Lalique in a daring early-morning raid on Sunday, just months after a stunning gem heist at the Louvre in Paris.

A gang of masked thieves broke in to the museum in Wingen-sur-Moder in northeastern France around 5:30 am, forcing a door before heading for the jewelry room and smashing open six display cases, a source close to the investigation told AFP.

nary_nodes.label: Stolen jewelry value assessed
evidence: "Around twenty pieces of jewelry were stolen. The loss is currently being assessed but could amount to several million euros, likely close to four million (over $4.5 million)," the source said.

nary_nodes.label: Stolen jewelry is crystal, not gems
evidence: Another source close to the investigation said the stolen jewelry was crystal, without precious gems, and could not be melted down.

nary_nodes.label: Lalique Museum closed due to burglary
evidence: The museum said on its website that it will be closed for several day because of the burglary.

nary_nodes.label: Alarm went off, cleaning lady called police
evidence: "An alarm went off, but by the time the security company had completed its checks, it was a cleaning lady who arrived first on the scene and called the police," the first investigation source added.

nary_nodes.label: CCTV footage being examined
evidence: The CCTV footage is currently being examined.

nary_nodes.label: Lalique Museum opened
evidence: The museum, dedicated to the Art Nouveau and Art Deco jeweler and glassmaker Rene Lalique, was opened in 2011 near the company's factory.

nary_nodes.label: Mayor angry about burglary
evidence: The mayor of Wingen-sur-Moder, a town of 1,500 inhabitants about 37 miles northwest of Strasbourg, told local newspaper Les Dernieres nouvelles d'Alsace (DNA) he was angry about the burglary.

nary_nodes.label: Security company had major failure
evidence: "All the alarms went off, just as they should. And then with the security company, apparently, there was a major failure on their part: they didn't intervene right away, they didn't inform the gendarmes," Christian Dorschner said.

nary_nodes.label: Burglars are specialists
evidence: "They were surely well informed to carry out this job in that way; they must be... specialists," the mayor also told DNA.

nary_nodes.label: Jewelry stolen from Louvre Museum
evidence: just months after a stunning gem heist at the Louvre in Paris.
Thieves made off with $102 million worth of jewelry, including some of the old French crown jewels, from the Louvre in a raid lasting less than eight minutes.

nary_nodes.label: Suspected thieves arrested and charged
evidence: The suspected thieves have been arrested and charged, but none of the jewels have been recovered except for a crown that was dropped as the group escaped.

nary_nodes.label: Most Louvre jewels not recovered
evidence: none of the jewels have been recovered except for a crown that was dropped as the group escaped.

nary_nodes.label: Security audit found unmonitored rooms
evidence: A security audit found that 35% of the rooms in the Denon Wing, where the stolen jewels were displayed, were not monitored by security cameras, according to Radio France.

nary_nodes.label: Gems not privately insured
evidence: The gems were also not privately insured, in accordance with French law.

nary_nodes.label: French museums suffered break-ins
evidence: France's museums have suffered a spate of break-ins in recent months.

nary_nodes.label: Gold stolen from Natural History Museum
evidence: Last October, a woman was arrested and charged over the theft of gold from the Natural History Museum in Paris.

nary_nodes.label: Porcelain works stolen from Adrien Dubouche Museum
evidence: In September, thieves snatched three porcelain works worth millions of dollars and classed as national treasures in a heist at the Adrien Dubouche National Museum in Limoges in central France.

nary_nodes.label: 18th-century works stolen from Cognacq-Jay Museum
evidence: In November 2024, four men with axes and baseball bats smashed the display cases in broad daylight at the Cognacq-Jay museum in Paris, making off with several 18th-century works.

nary_nodes.label: Insurance payment for Cognacq-Jay heist
evidence: That heist resulted in an insurance payment of over $4 million to the Royal Collection Trust, BBC News reported.

nary_nodes.label: Jewelry stolen from Saone-et-Loire museum
evidence: The next day, jewelry valued at several million dollars was stolen during an armed robbery at a museum in Saone-et-Loire in central France.
